kept.excerpt: Brazil's GDP grew 0.5% in the second quarter from the previous quarter, down from 1.1% in the first quarter but above the 0.4% forecast in a Reuters poll. Household consumption fell 0.4%, its first contraction in three quarters. The benchmark interest rate remained at 14%.
kept.relevance: The latest GDP release available before the cutoff documents slowing demand while showing that headline growth exceeded economists' expectations.

kept.excerpt: Brazil’s annual inflation rate decreased to 4.24% in early August, falling within the central bank’s tolerance range, according to official data released Wednesday. Consumer prices dropped 0.4% from the previous month, the data showed. The annual reading came in below the 4.33% median forecast, while the monthly decline exceeded the estimated 0.32% decrease.
kept.relevance: The inflation release available before the cutoff provides evidence of disinflation relevant to whether COPOM could continue reducing rates.

kept.excerpt: O Copom decidiu reduzir a taxa básica de juros para 14,00% a.a., e entende que essa decisão é compatível com a estratégia de convergência da inflação para o redor da meta ao longo do horizonte relevante. O cenário atual, caracterizado por significativo aumento da incerteza, desancoragem das expectativas e riscos elevados em torno do cenário base, demanda serenidade e cautela na condução da política monetária. O Comitê seguirá incorporando novas informações e acompanhando a evolução do cenário de forma a manter a restrição adequada para assegurar a convergência da inflação à meta.
kept.publisher: Banco Central do Brasil — Minutes of the 280th COPOM meeting
kept.relevance: The official minutes establish the prevailing target and COPOM's cautious, information-dependent policy stance before the September meeting.

kept.excerpt: Brazil's central bank cut interest rates by 25 basis points at a fourth straight policy meeting. COPOM unanimously cut the benchmark Selic rate to 14.00%, the lowest level since March 2025. The decision matched the expectations of 38 of 42 analysts polled by Reuters, with the remainder forecasting unchanged rates.
kept.relevance: The preceding decision establishes a recent pattern of quarter-point cuts and records the economist consensus at that meeting.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-09-02, inclusive. Six items were retained with verifiable publication dates on or before the cutoff; later-dated results, undated current-status pages, prediction-market pages, and live financial prices were excluded from the evidence pack. The institution responsible is Banco Central do Brasil, Brazil's central bank. Its dated calendar announcement schedules the September 2026 meeting for September 15–16, rather than September 14–15. Built-in web_fetch failed because multiple fetch providers were registered, so agent-reach web read was used to retrieve source text. The official minutes' displayed publication date is August 11, 2026; a later technical page timestamp was disregarded. The Jornal do Comércio publication date was verified on the page, while its quoted survey text was available in the indexed search result; the fetched page restricted the article body. English excerpts are concise factual renderings of the source text; Portuguese excerpts preserve the original wording. The Investing.com inflation article identifies itself as generated with AI support and reviewed by an editor. The Focus year-end median is not a meeting-specific forecast.
